## 📌 Description

Retain the settings and architecture requirements, remove repetition, and add a resource-lifetime review checklist.

Thank you for contributing to FlashInfer! Before we review your pull request, please make sure the following items are complete.

### ✅ Pre-commit Checks

- [x] I have installed `pre-commit` by running `pip install pre-commit` (or used your preferred method).
- [x] I have installed the hooks with `pre-commit install`.
- [ ] I have run the hooks manually with `pre-commit run --all-files` and fixed any reported issues.

Changed-file hooks passed; the full-repository hook run was not performed.

- [ ] Tests have been added or updated as needed.
- [ ] All tests are passing (`unittest`, etc.).
- [ ] This PR requires **full-scope** CI, not targeted tests (expensive; justify below).
      Reason: Not required for this documentation change.

+
+Apply these checks when designing or reviewing reuse, caching, or longer-lived

+
+- **Retained memory.** Measure CPU/GPU memory through compilation, profiling,

+  hardware/software versions, and measurement limitations.
+- **Cache growth.** Bound live resources across realistic key sequences,
+  devices, and concurrent sessions. A per-pool limit does not bound all pools.

+  keys. For example, workers reduce available memory; recalculating their count

+  headroom beside application allocations such as a vLLM KV cache. State when

+# Backend implementation notes
+
+Read the relevant contract before changing dispatch, captured-buffer lifetimes,
+or dtypes. General workflow rules are in [AGENTS.md](../../AGENTS.md).
+
+- [cuDNN linear attention](#cudnn-linear-attention)
+- [cuDNN query sparse attention](#cudnn-query-sparse-attention)
+- [Attention plans and CUDA graphs](#attention-plan-and-cuda-graph-lifetime)
+- [Grouped FP8 GEMM](#grouped-fp8-gemm)
+- [SM90 FP4 MegaMoE](#sm90-fp4-megamoe)
+- [Prims-TS decode dtypes](#prims-ts-decode-dtypes)
+
+## cuDNN linear attention
+
+Use `nvidia-cudnn-frontend>=1.32.0`; automatic selection also requires CuTe DSL
+4.7+. KDA/GDN normalization adds `1e-6`, without an epsilon argument. KDA's
+SM100/SM103 policies live in `flashinfer/kda.py`; GDN's SM100 policy lives in
+`flashinfer/gdn_prefill.py`. See [KDA shape regions](../api/kda.rst).
+
+Auto-selected cuDNN ignores the native KDA workspace; native fallback uses it.
+Explicit state-pool calls require unique, in-range slots, while automatic
+selection keeps pools on their native route. Validate outputs and final states
+when changing these policies.
+
+Use `benchmarks/bench_cudnn_linear_attention.py` for public-call comparisons.
+Its raw-gate GDN baseline includes Torch transforms, unlike a vLLM fused-producer
+baseline. Report host CPU, completed wall, and reset-inclusive CUDA graph times
+separately.
+
+## cuDNN query sparse attention
+
+Both APIs take BF16 Q/K/V. `flashinfer.qsa_forward` selects blocks with a packed
+`uint8` QSA block bitmap; `flashinfer.qsa_indexed_forward` accepts existing
+causal token IDs arranged in non-overlapping four-slot groups (a complete block,
+four `-1` padding slots, or a partial causal tail followed by `-1`). These
+device-value rules are a caller contract and are not checked on the host; see
+the docstrings in `flashinfer/qsa.py`. Both call
+`cudnn.ops`, return BF16 output, FP32 output, and natural-log LSE, and do not
+register autograd. Keep imports lazy and preserve these input/output contracts.
+
+Validate dispatch changes during CUDA graph replay. Indexed forward is not
+bitwise repeatable because index compaction can change accumulation order.
+On cuDNN Frontend 1.32, cover the bitmap boundary at 512/513 tokens.
+
+## Attention plan and CUDA Graph lifetime
+
+### Buffer ownership and graph bounds
+
+Old captures can retain a previous provider's metadata pointers after `auto`
+changes providers. Keep wrapper-owned tables and length buffers alive and
+refresh them in `plan()`, even when the page table is caller-owned. `run()` must
+not rebuild or repack metadata. Replay only with compatible buffers and lengths
+within the capture's declared bounds.
+
+A reserved table can exceed a capture's KV range. Declare only that range,
+preserving its storage row stride and pointer. Intersect the explicit KV maximum
+with caller-table capacity; use the same bound for the attention attribute and
+table slice. Device lengths still mask live tokens without host readback.
+Capacity must cover initialized indices and rounded graph bounds.
+
+Test changed page IDs and lengths, replacement by a caller table of another
+width, and Q-partition changes after a caller-owned first plan. Shortening a KV
+prefix alone can hide stale metadata. Include fallback beyond cuDNN admission
+and a backend-only provider control: FROST can accept oversized descriptors the
+backend rejects. Provider controls need an isolated real graph cache and a
+selected-engine check. Keep lifetime/numerical tests independent of heuristic
+winners and timing thresholds.
+
+### Ragged lengths and masks
+
+Valid attention lengths differ from physical ragged offsets: `seq_lens_q` can
+be shorter than its slot. Infer lengths from adjacent offsets only when omitted.
+Keep token-offset units consistent in graph descriptors and override shapes,
+regardless of whether masks use lengths or cumulative lengths.
+
+From the first graph-mode cuDNN plan, stage both mask lengths into owned
+storage, even when inferred. Replan with fresh caller tensors, alternating
+Q-only, KV-only, both, and omitted lengths. Replay the original capture against
+a compacted reference; checking only the latest eager call misses stale
+bindings and mask-representation transitions.
+
+### FA2 scheduling and runtime scales
+
+FA2 captures bind CPU-generated output/merge prefixes as well as indptr tensors.
+Updating indptrs after switching to cuDNN leaves schedules stale when requests
+exchange query rows. In graph mode, keep FA2 once planned; eager auto selection
+can still change providers. Test FA2-first and cuDNN-first sequences with changed
+Q partitions and page IDs.
+
+Preserve runtime calibration scales for half-precision and FP8 inputs. Test
+non-unit Q/K scales with nontrivial logits, V scaling of O with unchanged LSE,
+and GPU scalar updates before replay. Plan-time predicates cannot exclude
+arguments supplied only to `run()`.
+
+### Admission without host readback
+
+Declining cuDNN can make FA2 stage KV metadata back to the host. Use per-request
+work for admission only when its lengths are already on CPU; otherwise retain
+the bound-based policy. Check with a busy GPU stream and synchronization
+debugging, as well as predicate-level tests.
+
+Full-prefill admission requires each request's Q length to equal its KV length;
+equal batch maxima do not prove this. Use existing CPU metadata to establish
+that condition. Decline the extension if independent query-length overrides or
+device-only KV lengths prevent proof. Preserve the existing prefix policy
+without introducing a dispatch readback.
+
+## Grouped FP8 GEMM
+
+`flashinfer.gemm.group_gemm_fp8_nt_groupwise_contiguous` is the standalone
+CuTe-DSL API; `group_deepgemm_fp8_nt_groupwise` retains its DeepGEMM-only
+signature. Both use per-row expert indices, unlike the indptr-based
+`group_gemm_fp8_nt_groupwise` API.
+
+Use `python benchmarks/bench_grouped_fp8.py --production-shapes` to compare
+DeepGEMM/CuTe-DSL with preallocated outputs. `--cache-probe` separates first-call
+and new-token-count compilation. CuTe-DSL reuses kernels across token counts
+with the same 128-row alignment class, at most two variants per device/weight
+shape. Concurrent misses share compilation; warm hits avoid the compile lock.
+
+With `skip_check=False`, `validate_indices=True` checks routing values for
+non-empty inputs and synchronizes with the CPU. Validate new routing data before
+capture. The default checks metadata only; `skip_check=True` bypasses both
+metadata and routing-value checks, even when `validate_indices=True`.
+
+## SM90 FP4 MegaMoE
+
+For SM90 NVFP4 fused/split and MXFP4 fused MegaMoE, use
+[bench_megamoe_fp4_sm90.py](../../benchmarks/bench_megamoe_fp4_sm90.py) for
+timing and [test_megamoe_fp4_sm90.py](../../tests/moe/test_megamoe_fp4_sm90.py)
+for correctness checks.
+
+## Prims-TS decode dtypes
+
+Keep storage (`q_dtype`, `k_dtype`, `v_dtype`) separate from MMA precision
+(`qk_dtype`, `pv_dtype`). Transformed FP8/NVFP4 K/V uses Q's compute dtype;
+BF16 Q/K with FP8 V uses FP8 PV without that transform. Kernel predicates,
+P packing, and attention-sink scaling follow compute precision; TMA descriptors
+and allocations follow storage precision.
+
+`BatchDecodePagedTSWrapper.plan()` accepts `k_dtype`, `v_dtype`, and the common-KV
+alias `kv_dtype`. `BlockSparseTSWrapper.plan()` instead accepts `k_data_type`,
+`v_data_type`, and the common-KV alias `kv_data_type`. Use the names for the
+specific wrapper.

+
+General workflow rules live in [AGENTS.md](../../AGENTS.md).
+
+## Common controls
+
+Set API logging and tensor-dump controls before importing FlashInfer.
+
+| Variable | Purpose |
+| --- | --- |
+| `FLASHINFER_LOGLEVEL` | API logging: 0 off, 1 names, 3 inputs/outputs, 5 statistics, 10 tensor dumps |
+| `FLASHINFER_LOGDEST` | `stdout`, `stderr`, or an output file |
+| `FLASHINFER_JIT_VERBOSE` | `1` enables verbose build output; also enables nvcc debug builds if `FLASHINFER_JIT_DEBUG` is unset |
+| `FLASHINFER_JIT_DEBUG` | `1` enables debug symbols, `-O0`, and device debugging; `0` keeps verbose nvcc builds optimized |
+| `FLASHINFER_CUDA_ARCH_LIST` | Compilation targets, e.g. `8.0 9.0a` |
+| `FLASHINFER_NVCC_THREADS` | Threads per nvcc process |
+| `MAX_JOBS` | Parallel Ninja jobs |
+| `FLASHINFER_WORKSPACE_BASE` | Base for `.cache/flashinfer/` |
+
+Compilation memory grows with both `MAX_JOBS` and `FLASHINFER_NVCC_THREADS`.

+`load()`. Its shared `build_and_load()` handles caching, locking, and
+`FLASHINFER_DISABLE_JIT`. Toolchains implement that lifecycle:
+
+- `JitSpecNvcc`, returned by `gen_jit_spec()`, takes `name`, `sources`,
+  `extra_cuda_cflags`, `extra_cflags`, and `extra_ldflags`. It generates Ninja
+  rules, builds `.so` modules, and loads them through TVM-FFI.
+- `JitSpecCuteDsl` in `flashinfer/jit/cute_dsl_core.py` persists CuTe-DSL kernels.
+- The private TIRx spec in `flashinfer/kda_kernels/tirx/cache.py` fingerprints
+  sources/compiler and checks artifacts. TVM/TIRx imports occur only for an
+  explicit `recurrent_kda(..., backend="tirx")`; see [KDA](../api/kda.rst).
+
+Installed source/AOT directories may be read-only. Write generated artifacts to
+workspace paths:
+
+| Directory | Writable | Use for |
+|-----------|----------|---------|
+| `FLASHINFER_GEN_SRC_DIR` | ✓ Yes | Generated source files (Jinja output, copied .cu files) |
+| `FLASHINFER_JIT_DIR` | ✓ Yes | Compiled `.so` outputs |
+| `FLASHINFER_CSRC_DIR` | ✗ No | Read-only source templates |
+| `FLASHINFER_AOT_DIR` | ✗ No | Read-only pre-compiled binaries |
+
+`CompilationContext` detects GPUs or reads `FLASHINFER_CUDA_ARCH_LIST`.
+Generators constrain targets with `supported_major_versions`; no supported
+architecture raises `RuntimeError`. FP4 CuTe-DSL worker parallelism uses
+`FLASHINFER_MM_FP4_CUTE_DSL_COMPILE_WORKERS`.
+
+A `gen_*_module()` computes a parameter-specific URI, writes under
+`FLASHINFER_GEN_SRC_DIR / uri`, and returns `gen_jit_spec(...)`. Read templates
+from `csrc/`; render Jinja only for needed specialization and use
+`write_if_different()` to avoid unnecessary rebuilds. Follow existing
+`DISPATCH_DTYPE` / `DISPATCH_BLOCK_SIZE` macros for runtime specialization.
+
+## Module caching
+
+`@functools.cache` retains loaded modules in Python; the file cache under
+`~/.cache/flashinfer/` retains compiled artifacts. nvcc freshness relies on
+Ninja dependency/timestamp checks, not source-content hashes. Replacing a source
+with an older timestamp can therefore reuse a stale object. CuTe-DSL uses source
+hashes as described below. Set `FLASHINFER_WORKSPACE_BASE` to change the cache
+base; remove `~/.cache/flashinfer/` to clear the default cache.
+
+### CuTe-DSL artifacts and invalidation
+
+With caching enabled and hashable sources, `build_and_load_cute_dsl_kernel()`
+wraps `JitSpecCuteDsl`, exporting kernels with
+`export_to_c()` and reloading through
+`cute.runtime.load_module(..., enable_tvm_ffi=True)`. Each
+`cached_ops/<module>_<arch>_cute_dsl/` contains `meta.json` and one `.o` per
+specialization. These are single-architecture artifacts: the target comes from
+`CUTE_DSL_ARCH` or the current device, rather than an nvcc fatbin.
+
+Changes to DSL/Torch/TVM-FFI distributions, Python ABI, or kernel-source SHA256
+invalidate the module, which rebuilds lazily. See
+`flashinfer/quantization/kernels/nvfp4_quantize.py` for usage. Set
+`FLASHINFER_CUTE_DSL_DISABLE_CACHE=1` to disable persistence.
+
+### Source-key coverage
+
+By default, SHA256 covers the caller's `extra_key_files`, often just `__file__`.
+`FLASHINFER_CUTE_DSL_STRICT_CACHE_KEY=1` extends coverage to the in-package
+source dependencies. Analysis/hashing lives in `flashinfer/jit/_cute_dsl_source.py`;
+`cute_dsl_core.py` manages compilation and artifacts. Strict analysis follows:
+
+- Plain modules and their imports, including literal `importlib.import_module`
+  calls, keyed by content.
+- Package names through their defining bindings: re-exports to their source,
+  functions into their bodies, modules through accessed attributes, and the
+  submodule of the same name.
+- Initializer code executed at import, including evaluated function annotations,
+  for every keyed file in that package. Initializer keys cover this code and
+  import lines for used names; unused re-exports or `__all__` additions do not
+  invalidate artifacts.
+- Star imports when they can replace bindings, and lazy fallbacks when bindings
+  may be absent.
+
+Side effects of modules the keyed code neither imports nor uses, nonliteral
+dynamic imports, and runtime file reads are outside this analysis; supply files explicitly
+in `extra_key_files`. `version.py` and `_build_meta.py` are excluded so caches
+can survive checkout changes.
+
+Task-scheduled attention uses this cache through
+`flashinfer/attention/prims_ts/_compile_cache.py`. Its keys cover compile specs,
+options, embedded device-capacity constants, and the attention source tree,
+including shared preparation, masks, and reductions. `_hardware.py` caches
+occupancy queries per device and cluster size.
+
+## Compiler caches
+
+Devcontainers set `FLASHINFER_NVCC_LAUNCHER` / `FLASHINFER_CXX_LAUNCHER` to
+sccache; `~/.cache/sccache` is a volume that survives rebuilds. Inspect it with
+`sccache --show-stats`; clear a launcher variable to disable that path. Changing
+launchers changes Ninja commands and can rebuild objects. Linking, cubin
+embedding, and CuTe-DSL compilation bypass nvcc's sccache. Do not share one local
+sccache directory between containers.
+
+For persistent per-runner caches, S3 seeds, locking, pruning, and publication,
+follow [the CI cache contract](../../ci/COMPILE_CACHE.md).
+Runner cache budgets use `CI_COMPILE_CACHE_MAX_MB` (default 40960) and
+`CI_COMPILE_CACHE_MIN_FREE_MB` (default 20480); see
+[the implementation](../../ci/compile_cache.sh) for size/free-space handling.
+
+### CI wheel builds and test wrappers
+
+Release/nightly provider builds use server-side sccache and
+`scripts/build_jit_cache_wheel.py`. The script uses the container's torch-pinned
+interpreter: isolated-environment paths in TVM-FFI includes would change every
+sccache key. It also fixes installed-header mtimes. GCC's `#pragma once` can
+skip headers matching size, content, and mtime; byte-identical Torch
+`ATen/ops/*_native.h` stubs otherwise make preprocessing depend on pip timing.
+
+After 90 minutes without output, the watchdog records system, process, compiler,
+and sccache state, sends TERM to the build process group, then KILL after two
+minutes, and exits 124. Compiler discovery scans the container, including
+sccache-owned processes outside the group. `docker run --rm` provides final
+cleanup.
+
+PR GPU lanes use `scripts/run_with_test_sccache.sh` with the release/nightly
+AOT builds' S3 cache and prefix, publishing `sccache-stats-<kind>-<cuda>-<index>` artifacts. The
+repository variable `FLASHINFER_GPU_TEST_SCCACHE=0` disables it for comparisons;
+a failed sccache install falls back to an uncached lane. Server-owned compiles
+survive a unit's process-group kill; per-unit memory telemetry excludes nvcc. Locally, run
+`scripts/run_with_test_sccache.sh scripts/task_run_unit_tests.sh` (read-only
+without AWS credentials).
+
+### Provider architecture checks
+
+PR `AOT Build Import` applies release architecture rules: a module emitting a
+foreign provider's CUDA target or PTX fails validation. Before compilation,
+`scripts/check_jit_spec_gencodes.py --provider <arch>` generates specs through
+`flashinfer.aot.generate_jit_specs` and checks explicit `-gencode` flags with
+`provider_flag_issues` in `flashinfer/jit/_cuda_architecture.py`. This needs Torch
+and nvcc, not a GPU. Specs without explicit flags use the provider-filtered
+compilation context.
+
+`Provider Spec Lint (cuXXX)` runs `scripts/task_check_jit_spec_gencodes.sh` per
+CUDA image before AOT builds and participates in `Test Results Summary`; AOT
+lanes repeat the check. After wheel builds,
+`scripts/verify_jit_cache_provider_architectures.py` performs the release
+`cuobjdump` inspection. Register multi-architecture sources only for targets in
+`current_compilation_context.TARGET_CUDA_ARCHS`; see `gen_ulysses_lowp_module`.
+
+The PR AOT lane (`scripts/task_test_jit_cache_package_build_import.sh`) uses the
+pinned rapidsai/sccache fork for nvcc (`FLASHINFER_SCCACHE_NVCC_IMPL=rapids`, key
+prefix `<tag>-rapids`). Dependency-list hashing reduces recorded nvcc-hit host
+CPU cost from 7.4 to about 0.3 CPU-s. Host C++ stays uncached because the fork
+fails on `g++ -MMD` for files including `<vector>`. Use
+`FLASHINFER_SCCACHE_NVCC_IMPL=upstream` for comparisons.
+
+## Adding a new operation
+
+For stable CUDA operations, use the
+[kernel tutorial](../../.claude/skills/add-cuda-kernel/SKILL.md) and this checklist:
+
+1. Write raw-pointer kernels in `include/flashinfer/`, a launcher in `csrc/`,
+   and TVM-FFI exports in a `*_jit_binding.cu` file.
+2. Add a generator in `flashinfer/jit/`; use Jinja only if specialization needs it.
+3. Expose the Python API, cache its loaded modules with `@functools.cache`, and
+   export it from `flashinfer/__init__.py`.
+4. Add correctness tests, register in `flashinfer/aot.py`, and complete tracing
+   below. Experimental features follow their separate JIT-only policy.
+
+Examples: `flashinfer/norm/__init__.py` for a simple operation without Jinja,
+`flashinfer/sampling.py` for templating, and `flashinfer/decode.py` for plan/run
+and workspace management.
+
+### Trace templates for new or updated APIs
+
+Stable public APIs decorated with `@flashinfer_api` need a `trace=` template for
+`fi_trace()` and benchmark-definition dumps:
+
+1. Define/update `TraceTemplate` axes, inputs, outputs, and optional reference in
+   `flashinfer/trace/templates/<category>.py`. Wire it with
+   `@flashinfer_api(trace=my_trace)` on the function or class `run()` method.
+   When a module gains its first traced stable API, add it to
+   `_TRACE_REGISTRATION_MODULES` in `tests/trace/template_registry.py`; the
+   inventory test fails otherwise, and the generic template tests skip it.
+2. Add a realistic call to `tests/trace/example.py` and update its docstring's
+   output-file list.
+3. Regenerate into a scratch directory, for example
+   `PYTHONPATH=$PWD FLASHINFER_TRACE_DUMP_DIR=/tmp/fi_trace_new python tests/trace/example.py`,
+   then copy the new or intentionally changed JSON files into
+   `tests/trace/fi_trace_out/`. Do not delete that directory first: examples the
+   current GPU cannot run are skipped, and their committed files would be lost.
+   Run `pytest tests/trace/ -v` and commit the JSON files alongside the code.
+
+For an init shared by Const shapes, list keyword-only defaults in
+`init._trace_init_const_axes` so each definition binds its resolved Const values.
+Test exported snippets with only Var axes supplied; replay must not require
+callers to override Const defaults.
+
+## Building precompiled packages
+
+```bash
+# One binary provider for the target architecture.
+export FLASHINFER_JIT_CACHE_PROVIDER_ARCH=9.0a
+python -m build --no-isolation --wheel flashinfer-jit-cache-provider
+
+# Matching shim with exact provider dependencies.
+export FLASHINFER_JIT_CACHE_PROVIDER_ARCHS="9.0a"
+python -m build --no-isolation --wheel flashinfer-jit-cache
+```
+
+The provider runs registered `gen_*_module()` functions through
+`flashinfer/aot.py` for one architecture. The shim contains metadata and exact
+dependencies, not binaries. Keep `FLASHINFER_LOCAL_VERSION` and
+`FLASHINFER_DEV_RELEASE_SUFFIX` identical across matching provider/shim wheels.
+
+## Build implementation
+
+`build_backend.py` is the PEP 517 backend; `version.txt` produces
+`flashinfer/_build_meta.py`. Editable installs create these data symlinks:
+`3rdparty/cutlass` to `flashinfer/data/cutlass`, `csrc` to `flashinfer/data/csrc`,
+and `include` to `flashinfer/data/include`.
+
+`_flashinfer_filelock` uses Unix `fcntl.flock` or Portalocker's `Win32Locker`.
+Callers own opening, timeout policy, and cleanup; nonblocking contention raises
+`BlockingIOError`. Keeping the module top-level avoids GPU imports in standalone
+tools. Existing `filelock.FileLock` users retain their behavior.
+
+`build_backend.build_wheel` calls `_slim_wheel`: level-9 deflate, removal of
+vendored `3rdparty` Python trees swept up by package discovery, and optional
+experimental-source exclusion with `FLASHINFER_WHEEL_EXCLUDE_EXPERIMENTAL_SOURCES=1`
+in release builds, except the two HC JIT sources in `_EXPERIMENTAL_SOURCES_KEEP`.
+It regenerates RECORD. See `tests/cpu/infra/test_build_backend_slim_wheel.py`.
+
+## Bindings and dependencies
+
+Export framework-independent functions with
+`TVM_FFI_DLL_EXPORT_TYPED_FUNC(name, func)`. Torch custom operators provide
+`torch.compile()` / CUDA graph integration; build rules use Ninja.
+
+| Dependency | Reference |
+| --- | --- |
+| TVM-FFI | <https://tvm.apache.org/ffi/> |
+| CUTLASS | Prefer local `3rdparty/cutlass/` source; <https://github.com/NVIDIA/cutlass> |
+| CuTe DSL | <https://docs.nvidia.com/cutlass/latest/media/docs/pythonDSL/cute_dsl_general/dsl_introduction.html> |
+| PTX ISA | <https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/parallel-thread-execution/index.html.md> |

+CuTe DSL comes from `nvidia-cutlass-dsl`, separately from the CUTLASS submodule.
+Dependencies are declared in `requirements.txt` and `3rdparty/`; versioning
+follows [CONTRIBUTING.md](../../CONTRIBUTING.md#release-versioning).

+# Testing and resource scheduling
+
+Use the targeted commands in [AGENTS.md](../../AGENTS.md) for routine changes.
+This reference covers:
+
+- [CPU-only PR lane](#cpu-only-pr-lane)
+- [Runner scheduling](#sharded-test-runner)
+- [Resource telemetry](#resource-telemetry)
+- [Collection and completion reports](#collection-and-completion-reports)
+- [MXFP8 startup benchmark](#mxfp8-startup-benchmark)
+- [Architecture guards](#architecture-guards)
+
+## CPU-only PR lane
+
+Every public run that executes tests also runs all of `tests/cpu` in the
+"CPU Unittest" lane on a CPU runner, regardless of selected targets. These tests
+must not require a GPU; GPU lanes exclude them. Docs-only PRs run no tests, and
+`workflow_dispatch` with `skip_gpu` also drops the CPU lane.
+
+## Sharded test runner
+
+Run `pytest --confcutdir=tests/test_sharding tests/test_sharding/` for the
+CPU-only coordinator suite.
+
+The default is one worker per visible GPU. H100 PR CI uses
+`--workers-per-gpu 2` (eight workers on four GPUs); other lanes keep the default.
+Locally, use `scripts/task_run_unit_tests.sh --workers-per-gpu 2` for sharing or
+`--workers N` for a total count. Workers share the JIT compilation budget.
+The script prepares a CI container: it installs the Python requirements and the
+local package, and runs `apt-get` when `jq` is missing. Run it in a disposable
+container or environment, not in a development environment you want unchanged.
+
+### Scheduling and memory
+
+Scheduling markers apply to the whole source file:
+
+- `node_exclusive`: run alone across the allocation after parallel work, with
+  all GPUs visible. Use for multi-GPU requirements or host-memory OOM risk.
+- `gpu_exclusive`: run alone on the assigned GPU; other GPUs can keep working.
+- `host_memory_heavy`: prioritize this file and serialize its units with other
+  host-heavy work, while lighter files can overlap.
+
+Host/GPU reservations are acquired together and cover setup through cleanup.
+Blocked units stay queued; workers can run other work or steal from another
+queue. GPU-exclusive work can drain one GPU without holding the host-heavy slot
+or blocking other GPUs. `RESOURCE WAIT` reports idle periods of at least one
+second when queued work cannot use that worker's resources.
+
+Markers control overlap, not memory limits. Most H100 annotations reflect
+peaks above 128 GiB host RSS or 32 GiB GPU memory. Attention sink uses both
+narrower markers: 89.2 GiB host RSS and 4.5 GiB GPU on a single-GPU H100 run,
+allowing other GPUs to work. Cold JIT and other GPUs can change these peaks.
+For concurrency changes, compare completion rate, OOM failures, and repeated
+wall times with matching scope and cache conditions.
+
+Capacity reports include the host-heavy/node-exclusive serial floor, but use
+worker counts without topology or measured memory capacity. Treat their GPU
+contention estimates as optimistic.
+
+## Resource telemetry
+
+Allocation telemetry defaults to a 5-second interval (`RESOURCE_MONITOR_INTERVAL`);
+per-batch sampling defaults to 2 seconds (`MEMORY_MONITOR_INTERVAL`).
+`resource_monitor.py` separates sampling, CSV persistence, and aggregation;
+allocation/batch monitors share `scripts/test_sharding/host_cpu.py` readers.
+Unavailable per-process GPU memory stays unknown and marks source summaries
+partial; `memory_summary.csv` leaves maxima blank without valid observations.
+Host rows flush before GPU queries, whose costs appear in `sampler.csv`.
+Nested runners reuse samplers only while the exported owner PID lives.
+Attribute namespace-relative cgroup paths only with membership evidence.
+
+## Collection and completion reports
+
+Public CI uploads collection stdout/stderr and best-effort JIT prewarm warnings
+from `junit/collection-*/*.log`. Separate directories preserve concurrent and
+previous attempts' diagnostics; collection metadata remains temporary.
+
+Set `UNIT_TEST_RUN_STATUS_DIR` to a fresh directory unique to each
+communication-test wrapper and container/rank to enable completion reports.
+`test_run_status.sh` records pytest invocations; `test_run_status.py` atomically
+writes `script-result.json` with schema version 1, `complete`, `exit_code`,
+`tests_executed`, and `infrastructure_errors`. A pytest plugin records execution,
+collection, and internal errors inside each MPI/torchrun worker. Launcher exit
+1 alone does not prove an assertion failure.
+
+Cache publication requires every local worker rank to finish and at least one
+test to execute. Completed assertion failures remain eligible; crashes, timeouts,
+and unfinished invocations do not. Unsetting the variable disables reports,
+while missing JUnit output and file timeouts still fail the wrapper. The CPU
+coordinator suite covers this contract without GPUs.
+
+## MXFP8 startup benchmark
+
+Run `python benchmarks/bench_mxfp8_startup.py --output-dir /path/to/new/results` on
+B200/B300 to compare persistence disabled, serial/parallel disk-cache population,
+fresh-process disk hits, and saved tuning winners. The benchmark isolates caches
+and checks results after CUDA graph replay. Default shapes exercise the
+SM100-family persistent/split-K runner; see
+[cache scope and layers](../design_docs/cute_dsl_kernel_cache.md).
+
+MXFP8 precompile workers use a dedicated interpreter entry point. They do not
+rerun application scripts or require callers to add a `__main__` guard.
+
+## Architecture guards
+
+FlashInfer supports NVIDIA SM75, SM80, SM86, SM89, SM90, SM100, SM103, SM110,
+SM120, and SM121. Support varies by operation and backend.
+
+Use `flashinfer.utils.get_compute_capability(device)` for `(major, minor)`
+checks and the feature helpers for architecture-specific kernels:
+`is_sm90a_supported`, `is_sm100a_supported`, `is_sm100f_supported`,
+`is_sm110a_supported`, `is_sm120a_supported`, `is_sm120f_supported`, and
+`is_sm121a_supported`.
+
+Common architecture checks for specific kernel paths:
+
+| Kernel path | Architecture requirement | Guard |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| FlashAttention-3 | SM90a, CUDA 12.3+ | `is_sm90a_supported(device)` |
+| SM100a MLA attention | SM100a, CUDA 12.8+ | `is_sm100a_supported(device)` |
+| FP8 GEMM hardware support | SM89+ | `get_compute_capability(device) >= (8, 9)` |
+
+These checks do not replace an API's backend-support checks or its dtype and
+shape requirements.
+
+For example, guard a Hopper-specific test with:
+
+```python
+import pytest
+import torch
+
+from flashinfer.utils import is_sm90a_supported
+
+
+def test_hopper_attention():
+    if not is_sm90a_supported(torch.device("cuda")):
+        pytest.skip("Requires SM90a")
+    # Test the operation here.
+```
+
+APIs decorated with `@backend_requirement` expose
+`is_compute_capability_supported(cc)` and `is_backend_supported(backend, cc)`.
+`cc` is an integer, `major * 10 + minor` (e.g. `90`), not the tuple returned by
+`get_compute_capability`. Without `cc`, `is_backend_supported` only reports
+whether the backend name is registered, not whether it runs on the current GPU;
+pass `cc` in architecture guards. Use these checks rather than assuming all
+backends support an architecture. Self-validating modes that
+replace backend selection, such as `batch_invariant=True` in `mm_bf16`,
+`bmm_fp8`, `mm_mxfp8`, and `mm_fp4`, use the decorator's `bypass=` predicate;
+see the kernel tutorial.
+
+Choose problem sizes that avoid OOM; the OOM handling in `tests/conftest.py`
+is a fallback, not a sizing policy.

# CI workflow using AWS self-hosted runners.
# Runs AOT build tests, GPU unit tests and the CPU-only tests/cpu suite on PRs
# to main, and on main itself on a schedule.
# Uses ci/bash.sh for Docker execution (same as Jenkins).
#
# Permission Control:
# - main: a scheduled full-suite run three times a day (not per merge). Per-merge
#   runs shared one cancel-in-progress group, so each merge cancelled the last:
#   about 90% of them never finished. A scheduled run is never cancelled, runs
#   every lane to completion (no fail-fast), and a failure opens or updates a
#   tracking issue; the next green run closes it.
# - PRs: run when 'run-ci' or the bot's 'run-ci-focused' label is applied.
#   Applying the label is the trigger, so new commits need a new trigger:
#   @flashinfer-bot run.
#
# Instance Purchasing:
# - All runners are on-demand. Spot was removed.
# - A failure here is a real failure, so there is nothing to retry
#   automatically.
# - On-demand capacity is billed for as long as it runs, so the first failure
#   should stop everything else. GitHub only fail-fasts within one matrix, so
#   all tests live in a single matrix built by the setup job. They still start
#   in parallel; the matrix exists purely to make the cancellation global.

name: PR Test

on:
  # Off the 00:00 UTC nightly-release slot; one run per Asia / EU / US workday.
  # Minute 17, not 0: GitHub delays or drops scheduled runs at the top of the hour.
  schedule:
    - cron: '17 4,12,20 * * *'
  pull_request:
    branches: [main]
    types: [opened, synchronize, reopened, labeled, ready_for_review]
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      skip_aot:
        description: 'Skip AOT build tests'
        type: boolean
        default: false
      skip_gpu:
        description: 'Skip GPU tests'
        type: boolean
        default: false

concurrency:
  # A label other than run-ci can never start tests, so it gets its own group and
  # does not cancel - otherwise label churn would discard running GPU jobs.
  # Scheduled runs on main get their own group and never cancel each other: at
  # most one runs and one waits, so a slow run delays the next instead of wasting
  # itself.
  group: pr-test-${{ github.event_name == 'schedule' && 'scheduled-' || '' }}${{ github.ref }}${{ (github.event.action == 'labeled' && github.event.label.name != 'run-ci' && github.event.label.name != 'run-ci-focused') && '-noop' || '' }}
  cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.event_name != 'schedule' && !(github.event.action == 'labeled' && github.event.label.name != 'run-ci' && github.event.label.name != 'run-ci-focused') }}

permissions:
  contents: read
  pull-requests: write
  statuses: read # reads the ci/test-scope status published by ci-bot-commands.yml
  actions: read

env:
  EXECUTOR_NUMBER: "0"
  SKIP_CI_PATTERNS: '\.md$|^docs/|^docker/|^licenses/|^LICENSE$|^NOTICE$|^benchmarks/|^\.github/CODEOWNERS$'

jobs:
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Gate - Check if PR is authorized to run CI
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  gate:
    name: Permission Check
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    outputs:
      authorized: ${{ steps.check.outputs.authorized }}
    steps:
      - name: Check authorization
        id: check
        env:
          # Read via env, not inlined: a label name is caller-supplied text.
          EVENT_ACTION: ${{ github.event.action }}
          LABEL_NAME: ${{ github.event.label.name }}
        run: |
          # Always allow scheduled runs on main and workflow_dispatch
          if [[ "${{ github.event_name }}" != "pull_request" ]]; then
            echo "authorized=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "Not a PR, authorized"
            exit 0
          fi

          # Authorize on run-ci being applied, not on it being present: presence
          # would re-authorize every later push, which is the auto-trigger this
          # gate removes.
          if [[ "$EVENT_ACTION" == "labeled" && ( "$LABEL_NAME" == "run-ci" || "$LABEL_NAME" == "run-ci-focused" ) ]]; then
            echo "authorized=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "$LABEL_NAME label applied, authorized"
            exit 0
          fi

          echo "authorized=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "Not triggered by the run-ci label, skipping CI"

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Setup - Read docker tag and check if build should be skipped
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  setup:
    name: Setup
    needs: gate
    if: needs.gate.outputs.authorized == 'true'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    outputs:
      docker_tag: ${{ steps.get-tag.outputs.tag }}
      skip_build: ${{ steps.check.outputs.skip }}
      test_matrix: ${{ steps.matrix.outputs.matrix }}
      test_count: ${{ steps.matrix.outputs.count }}
      # Surfaced so the required check can say a green result was scoped.
      test_scope: ${{ steps.scope.outputs.test_path }}
      h100_disabled: ${{ steps.matrix.outputs.h100_disabled }}
      spec_lint_matrix: ${{ steps.matrix.outputs.spec_lint_matrix }}
      spec_lint_count: ${{ steps.matrix.outputs.spec_lint_count }}
      checkout_sha: ${{ steps.scope.outputs.checkout_sha || github.sha }}
      snapshot_base: ${{ steps.scope.outputs.snapshot_base }}
      snapshot_tree: ${{ steps.scope.outputs.snapshot_tree }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v5
        with:
          ref: ${{ github.sha }}
          fetch-depth: 0
          persist-credentials: false

      # Built here rather than written inline in the test job because the
      # `@flashinfer-bot run <paths>` publishes the requested scope as a `ci/test-scope`
      # commit status on this SHA (see ci-bot-commands.yml). Read it verbatim - the
      # comment was parsed once, there, and nothing is re-parsed here.
      #
      # Statuses come back newest-first, so the newest for this context is the last
      # command issued. No status means nobody asked for a scope: run the full suite.
      # Because the status is keyed to the SHA, a scope cannot outlive the commit it was
      # requested for.
      - name: Read requested test scope
        id: scope
        if: github.event_name == 'pull_request'
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          HEAD_SHA: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
          EVENT_SHA: ${{ github.sha }}
          REQUIRE_SNAPSHOT: ${{ github.event.label.name == 'run-ci-focused' }}
        run: |
          # The combined endpoint (/status, not /statuses) returns one entry per
          # context, already the latest. Using it means re-triggering overwrites
          # cleanly without this step deduplicating by hand, and without depending on
          # the raw list's ordering, which is not a documented guarantee.
          STATUSES=$(gh api "repos/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}/commits/${HEAD_SHA}/status")
          SCOPE=$(jq -r '
              .statuses
              | map(select(.context | test("^ci/test-scope-[0-9]+$")))
              | map({n: (.context | sub("^ci/test-scope-"; "") | tonumber),
                     d: (.description // "")})
              | sort_by(.n) | map(.d) | map(select(. != "")) | join(" ")' <<< "$STATUSES")

            echo "::error::Automatic test snapshot was cleared or is missing. Issue a new bot run command."
            exit 1
          fi
          if [ -n "$SNAPSHOT" ]; then
            if [[ ! "$SNAPSHOT" =~ ^[0-9a-f]{40}\ [0-9a-f]{40}\ [0-9a-f]{40}\ [0-9a-f]{16}$ ]]; then
              echo "::error::Invalid automatic test snapshot. Issue a new bot run command."
              exit 1
            fi
            read -r SELECTED_BASE SELECTED_MERGE SELECTED_TREE SELECTED_SCOPE <<< "$SNAPSHOT"
            ACTUAL_SCOPE=$(printf '%s' "$SCOPE" | sha256sum | cut -c1-16)
            if [ "$ACTUAL_SCOPE" != "$SELECTED_SCOPE" ]; then
              echo "::error::The automatic scope does not match its snapshot. Issue a new bot run command."
              exit 1
            fi
            # Reconstruct the selected source independently of GitHub's merge ref.
            # No PR scripts, hooks, or submodule contents run during preparation.
            for sha in "$SELECTED_BASE" "$HEAD_SHA"; do
              git cat-file -e "${sha}^{commit}" 2>/dev/null || git fetch --no-tags origin "$sha"
            done
            git -c core.hooksPath=/dev/null checkout --detach "$SELECTED_BASE"
            GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1 \
              git -c user.name=flashinfer-ci -c user.email=flashinfer-ci@nvidia.com \
              -c core.hooksPath=/dev/null -c rerere.enabled=false \
              merge --no-ff --no-edit "$HEAD_SHA"
            ACTUAL_TREE=$(git rev-parse 'HEAD^{tree}')
            if [ "$ACTUAL_TREE" != "$SELECTED_TREE" ]; then
              echo "::error::Merged source differs from AI-selected tree. Issue a new bot run command."
              exit 1
            fi
            echo "Verified AI-selected tree $ACTUAL_TREE (selection $SELECTED_MERGE)"
            echo "checkout_sha=${HEAD_SHA}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "snapshot_base=${SELECTED_BASE}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "snapshot_tree=${SELECTED_TREE}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          else
            echo "checkout_sha=${EVENT_SHA}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi
          if [ -z "$SCOPE" ]; then
            echo "No requested scope for ${HEAD_SHA}; running the full suite"
          else
            echo "Requested scope: ${SCOPE}"
          fi
          echo "test_path=${SCOPE}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

      - name: Validate CUDA configuration
        run: python3 ci/validate_cuda_versions.py

      # A shard script that no longer parses fails here, on the PR that changed it,
      # instead of silently un-scheduling later targeted A10G/T4 runs.
      - name: Validate bare-run coverage parse
        run: |
          python3 scripts/infra/pr_checks/targeted_lane_scope.py --coverage-only \

      - name: Get Docker Tag
        id: get-tag
        run: |
          TAG=$(grep 'flashinfer/flashinfer-ci-cu129:' ci/docker-tags.yml | cut -d':' -f2 | tr -d ' ')

            # tests/cpu runs on every run, whatever scope was requested. Its
            # tests check contracts across modules (package parity, stub
            # configs, wrapper attributes), so a change in one directory breaks
            # a CPU test that a scope naming that directory would not select.
            # It needs no GPU and takes about 5 minutes on a CPU runner, and
            # through fail-fast it stops the GPU lanes early when it fails.
            # The GPU lanes leave it out: the H100 lane ignores tests/cpu and
            # the A10G/T4 shard lists name no file under it.
            if [ "$SKIP_GPU" != "true" ]; then
              jq -nc '{
                name: "CPU Unittest",
                kind: "cpu",
                gpu_name: "CPU",
                runner: ["self-hosted", "linux", "x64", "cpu", "on-demand"],
                cuda: "cu129",
                script: "task_run_unit_tests.sh",
                test_path: "tests/cpu",
                timeout: 60
              }'
            fi

            if [ "$SKIP_GPU" != "true" ] && [ -z "${REQUESTED_TEST_PATH}" ]; then
              for shard in 1 2 3 4 5; do
                jq -nc --arg shard "$shard" '{
                  name: "JIT Unittest \($shard) (A10G)",
                  kind: "gpu",
                  gpu_name: "A10G",
                  runner: ["self-hosted", "linux", "x64", "gpu", "sm86", "on-demand"],
                  cuda: "cu129",
                  script: "task_jit_run_tests_part\($shard).sh",
                  timeout: 360
                }'
              done

              jq -nc '{
                name: "JIT Unittest (T4)",
                kind: "gpu",
                gpu_name: "T4",
                runner: ["self-hosted", "linux", "x64", "gpu", "sm75", "on-demand"],
                cuda: "cu129",
                script: "task_jit_run_tests_t4.sh",
                timeout: 360
              }'

              if [ "$RUN_H100" = "true" ]; then
                jq -nc '{
                  name: "JIT Unittest (H100)",
                  kind: "h100",
                  gpu_name: "H100",
                  runner: ["self-hosted", "linux", "x64", "gpu", "h100"],
                  cuda: "cu129",
                  script: "task_run_unit_tests.sh",
                  timeout: 480
                }'
              fi
            elif [ "$SKIP_GPU" != "true" ]; then
              # A `@flashinfer-bot run <paths>` comment retargets the GPU lanes at those
              # paths. There is deliberately no arch selection: tests carry their own
              # arch guards (is_sm90a_supported() and friends) and skip themselves where
              # unsupported - nobody has to keep a path-to-arch mapping in sync with the
              # tests. Per-lane scopes (A10G_SCOPES / T4_SCOPE) are computed above the
              # brace group, which is piped into jq and so runs in a subshell.
              #
              # A10G runs its bare-run shard scripts, restricted to the scope through
              # JIT_TEST_SCOPE (see scripts/infra/jit_test_logging.sh). T4 and H100 use
              # task_run_unit_tests.sh, the script that forwards "$@" into TEST_PATH.
              #
              # This step does NOT parse the PR body. Turning a declared scope into paths
              # happens once, in whoever issues the trigger (a reviewer, or the screening
              # watcher posting under its own identity). CI runs what it is told.
              for shard in 1 2 3 4 5; do
                if [ -n "${A10G_SCOPES[$shard]:-}" ]; then
                  jq -nc --arg shard "$shard" --arg test_path "${A10G_SCOPES[$shard]}" '{
                    name: "Targeted Unittest \($shard) (A10G)",
                    kind: "gpu",
                    gpu_name: "A10G",
                    runner: ["self-hosted", "linux", "x64", "gpu", "sm86", "on-demand"],
                    cuda: "cu129",
                    script: "task_jit_run_tests_part\($shard).sh",
                    test_path: $test_path,
                    timeout: 360
                  }'
                fi
              done
              if [ -n "${T4_SCOPE}" ]; then
                jq -nc --arg test_path "${T4_SCOPE}" '{
                  name: "Targeted Unittest (T4)",
                  kind: "gpu",
                  gpu_name: "T4",
                  runner: ["self-hosted", "linux", "x64", "gpu", "sm75", "on-demand"],
                  cuda: "cu129",
                  script: "task_run_unit_tests.sh",
                  test_path: $test_path,
                  timeout: 360
                }'
              fi
              if [ "$RUN_H100" = "true" ] && [ -n "${H100_SCOPE}" ]; then
                jq -nc --arg test_path "${H100_SCOPE}" '{
                  name: "Targeted Unittest (H100)",
                  kind: "h100",
                  gpu_name: "H100",
                  runner: ["self-hosted", "linux", "x64", "gpu", "h100"],
                  cuda: "cu129",
                  script: "task_run_unit_tests.sh",
                  test_path: $test_path,
                  timeout: 480
                }'
              fi
            fi
          } | jq -sc '{include: .}' > matrix.json

          echo "matrix=$(cat matrix.json)" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
          echo "count=$(jq '.include | length' matrix.json)" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
          jq -r '.include[].name' matrix.json

          # Provider spec lint: one quick lane per published CUDA image, ahead of the
          # hours-long AOT builds it guards, so a spec naming a CUDA target its
          # provider cannot carry fails the PR in minutes. Dropped with the AOT lanes.
          {
            if [ "$SKIP_AOT" != "true" ]; then
              for cuda in $(jq -r '.[].label' <<< "${RUNTIME_CUDA_MATRIX}"); do
                if grep -q "^flashinfer/flashinfer-ci-${cuda}:" ci/docker-tags.yml; then
                  jq -nc --arg cuda "$cuda" '{cuda: $cuda}'
                fi
              done
            fi
          } | jq -sc '{include: .}' > spec-lint-matrix.json
          echo "spec_lint_matrix=$(cat spec-lint-matrix.json)" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "spec_lint_count=$(jq '.include | length' spec-lint-matrix.json)" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Tests - AOT build imports and GPU unit tests
  #
  # Every test is one entry of a single matrix so that fail-fast cancels all of
  # them on the first failure. As separate jobs, fail-fast is scoped per group
  # and the other groups keep running on billed on-demand capacity long after
  # the result is known. Entries still start in parallel; nothing is serialized.
  # Scheduled runs on main turn fail-fast off: they exist to report every broken
  # lane, not the first one.
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  test:
    name: ${{ matrix.name }}
    needs: [gate, setup]
    if: |
      needs.gate.outputs.authorized == 'true' &&
      needs.setup.outputs.skip_build != 'true' &&
      needs.setup.outputs.test_count != '0'
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.runner }}
    timeout-minutes: ${{ matrix.timeout }}
    permissions:
      contents: read
      actions: read
      # Scheduled runs on main request the compile-cache upload role (see
      # "Get compile cache upload credentials"). The role's trust policy, not
      # this file, restricts it to refs/heads/main: a pull request run, even
      # one that edits this workflow, gets a token whose subject the policy
      # rejects.
      id-token: write
    strategy:
      fail-fast: ${{ github.event_name != 'schedule' }}
      matrix: ${{ fromJSON(needs.setup.outputs.test_matrix) }}
    env:
      DOCKER_IMAGE: flashinfer/flashinfer-ci-${{ matrix.cuda }}:${{ needs.setup.outputs.docker_tag }}
      MATRIX_ARCH: ${{ matrix.runner[2] }}
      MATRIX_CUDA: ${{ matrix.cuda }}
      CI_GPU_NAME: ${{ matrix.gpu_name }}
      MATRIX_KIND: ${{ matrix.kind }}
      TEST_SCRIPT: ${{ matrix.script }}
      # Empty for every lane except the experimental one. Quoted at the use site and
      # never interpolated into script text - it originates from the PR body.
      TEST_PATH_ARG: ${{ matrix.test_path }}
      # GPU lanes route their JIT compiles through the AOT lanes' S3 sccache.
      # On unless the repository variable FLASHINFER_GPU_TEST_SCCACHE is '0',
      # which turns it off for A/B timing without a code change. The `|| '1'`
      # matters: an unset variable is null, and `null != '0'` is false because
      # mismatched types are compared as numbers (null and '0' both become 0).
      # The CPU lane compiles nothing, so it skips sccache too.
      GPU_TEST_SCCACHE: ${{ matrix.kind != 'aot' && matrix.kind != 'cpu' && (vars.FLASHINFER_GPU_TEST_SCCACHE || '1') != '0' && '1' || '0' }}
    steps:
      - name: Cleanup
        if: matrix.kind != 'h100'
        run: |
          # Stop all Docker containers to free memory
          docker stop $(docker ps -q) 2>/dev/null || true
          docker rm $(docker ps -aq) 2>/dev/null || true
          # Clean workspace and caches
          sudo rm -rf ${{ github.workspace }}/* || true
          sudo rm -rf ${{ github.workspace }}/.[!.]* || true
          rm -rf ~/.cache/flashinfer_jit || true
          docker image prune -f || true
          docker builder prune -f --filter "until=24h" || true
          nvidia-smi || true

      - name: Cleanup
        if: matrix.kind == 'h100'
        run: |
          # Shared multi-runner node: only stop containers started by THIS runner (identified by workspace mount)
          for cid in $(docker ps -q); do
            if docker inspect "$cid" --format '{{json .Mounts}}' 2>/dev/null | grep -qF "${{ github.workspace }}/"; then
              docker stop "$cid" 2>/dev/null || true
            fi
          done
          sudo rm -rf ${{ github.workspace }}/* || true
          sudo rm -rf ${{ github.workspace }}/.[!.]* || true
          rm -rf ~/.cache/flashinfer_jit || true
          docker container prune -f 2>/dev/null || true
          docker image prune -f || true
          docker builder prune -f --filter "until=24h" || true
          echo "CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=$CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES"
          nvidia-smi -i "$CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES" || true

      - uses: actions/checkout@v5
        with:
          ref: ${{ needs.setup.outputs.checkout_sha }}
          # Self-hosted runners keep the workspace between jobs, so the token
          # must not be left behind in .git/config. Nothing here uses git after
          # checkout. Submodules initialize after source snapshot verification.
          persist-credentials: false

      - name: Prepare selected source and submodules
        env:
          SELECTED_BASE: ${{ needs.setup.outputs.snapshot_base }}
          SELECTED_TREE: ${{ needs.setup.outputs.snapshot_tree }}
        run: |
          if [ -n "$SELECTED_BASE" ]; then
            [[ "$SELECTED_BASE" =~ ^[0-9a-f]{40}$ && "$SELECTED_TREE" =~ ^[0-9a-f]{40}$ ]]
            PINNED_HEAD=$(git rev-parse HEAD)
            if [ "$(git rev-parse --is-shallow-repository)" = true ]; then
              git fetch --no-tags --unshallow origin "$PINNED_HEAD" "$SELECTED_BASE"
            fi
            git cat-file -e "${SELECTED_BASE}^{commit}" 2>/dev/null || git fetch --no-tags origin "$SELECTED_BASE"
            git -c core.hooksPath=/dev/null checkout --detach "$SELECTED_BASE"
            GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1 \
              git -c user.name=flashinfer-ci -c user.email=flashinfer-ci@nvidia.com \
              -c core.hooksPath=/dev/null -c rerere.enabled=false \
              merge --no-ff --no-edit "$PINNED_HEAD"
            [ "$(git rev-parse 'HEAD^{tree}')" = "$SELECTED_TREE" ]
          fi
          git submodule update --init --recursive

      - name: Show Node Info
        run: ./scripts/infra/task_show_node_info.sh
        env:
          NODE_NAME: ${{ runner.name }}
          WORKSPACE: ${{ github.workspace }}
          BUILD_NUMBER: ${{ github.run_number }}

      - name: Run Test
        if: matrix.kind == 'aot'
        env:
          SCCACHE_BUCKET: ${{ vars.SCCACHE_BUCKET }}
          SCCACHE_REGION: ${{ vars.SCCACHE_REGION }}
          AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID: ${{ secrets.SCCACHE_AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID }}
          AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY: ${{ secrets.SCCACHE_AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY }}
          # Provider builds overlapped per job (see the script). The repository
          # variable AOT_PROVIDER_CONCURRENCY overrides it, and 1 restores the
          # serial loop, for A/B timing without a code change.
          AOT_PROVIDER_CONCURRENCY: ${{ vars.AOT_PROVIDER_CONCURRENCY || '2' }}
        run: |
          if [ "${TEST_SCRIPT}" != "task_test_jit_cache_package_build_import.sh" ]; then
            echo "::error::Unexpected AOT test script: ${TEST_SCRIPT}"
            exit 1
          fi
          mkdir -p "${GITHUB_WORKSPACE}/sccache-stats"
          bash ci/bash.sh "${DOCKER_IMAGE}" \
            -e SCCACHE_BUCKET "${SCCACHE_BUCKET}" \
            -e SCCACHE_REGION "${SCCACHE_REGION}" \
            -e AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID \
            -e AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY \
            -e SCCACHE_STATS_DIR /workspace/sccache-stats \
            -e AOT_PROVIDER_CONCURRENCY "${AOT_PROVIDER_CONCURRENCY}" \
            --no-gpu "./scripts/infra/${TEST_SCRIPT}"

      - name: Configure compile cache
        if: matrix.kind != 'aot' && matrix.kind != 'cpu'
        env:
          S3_BUCKET: ${{ vars.SCCACHE_BUCKET || 'flashinfer-build-cache' }}
          S3_REGION: ${{ vars.SCCACHE_REGION || 'us-west-2' }}
          UPLOAD_ROLE: ${{ vars.COMPILE_CACHE_S3_ROLE_ARN }}
        run: |
          # Shared S3 layer of the compile cache (see ci/compile_cache_s3.sh):
          # one tarball per CI image ID, GPU and lane. A10G shards test different
          # files, so each shard is its own lane; targeted runs share the lane
          # of the bare run they narrow.
          case "${TEST_SCRIPT}" in
            task_jit_run_tests_part[1-5].sh) LANE="${TEST_SCRIPT#task_jit_run_tests_}"; LANE="${LANE%.sh}" ;;
            *) LANE=all ;;
          esac
          if [ -n "${S3_BUCKET}" ] && [ -n "${S3_REGION}" ]; then
            echo "CI_COMPILE_CACHE_S3_URL=https://${S3_BUCKET}.s3.${S3_REGION}.amazonaws.com/compile-cache/main" >> "${GITHUB_ENV}"
            echo "CI_COMPILE_CACHE_S3_LANE=${CI_GPU_NAME}/${LANE}" >> "${GITHUB_ENV}"
            # Only scheduled runs on main write, and only once an admin has
            # created the upload role. A writer compiles in a directory no
            # earlier job on this runner (any of them a pull request) can have
            # touched: a new path per job, and no shared pip cache, which PR
            # containers write as root.
            if [ "${GITHUB_EVENT_NAME}" = "schedule" ] && [ "${GITHUB_REF}" = "refs/heads/main" ] \
                && [ -n "${UPLOAD_ROLE}" ]; then
              echo "CI_COMPILE_CACHE_WRITER_DIR=$(mktemp -u "${RUNNER_TEMP}/compile-cache-writer.XXXXXXXX")" >> "${GITHUB_ENV}"
              echo "CI_PIP_CACHE_DIR=" >> "${GITHUB_ENV}"
            fi
          fi

      - name: Run Test
        if: matrix.kind != 'aot'
        env:
          SCCACHE_BUCKET: ${{ vars.SCCACHE_BUCKET }}
          SCCACHE_REGION: ${{ vars.SCCACHE_REGION }}
          AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID: ${{ env.GPU_TEST_SCCACHE == '1' && secrets.SCCACHE_AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID || '' }}
          AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY: ${{ env.GPU_TEST_SCCACHE == '1' && secrets.SCCACHE_AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY || '' }}
          # Kernel compile cache kept across this runner's jobs (see ci/bash.sh).
          # runner.workspace is the parent of the checkout, so the Cleanup step's
          # wipe of the checkout leaves it, and on the H100 hosts it sits on the
          # large NVMe work volume rather than the small root filesystem.
          CI_COMPILE_CACHE_DIR: ${{ runner.workspace }}/flashinfer-compile-cache
          CI_COMPILE_CACHE_RUNNER: ${{ runner.name }}
          # PR/manual runs consume private copies. Only scheduled runs on main
          # update seeds; main has no push trigger, so a push condition here
          # would leave every seed empty.
          CI_COMPILE_CACHE_MODE: ${{ github.event_name == 'schedule' && github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' && 'read-write' || 'read-only' }}
        run: |
          case "${TEST_SCRIPT}" in
            task_jit_run_tests_part[1-5].sh|task_jit_run_tests_t4.sh|task_run_unit_tests.sh) ;;
            *)
              echo "::error::Unexpected GPU test script: ${TEST_SCRIPT}"
              exit 1
              ;;
          esac
          # ci/bash.sh options must precede the command. The credentials are
          # forwarded by name so ci/bash.sh never echoes their values.
          DOCKER_ARGS=()
          LANE_COMMAND=("./scripts/infra/${TEST_SCRIPT}")
          if [ "${GPU_TEST_SCCACHE}" = "1" ]; then
            mkdir -p "${GITHUB_WORKSPACE}/sccache-stats"
            DOCKER_ARGS+=(
              -e SCCACHE_BUCKET "${SCCACHE_BUCKET}"
              -e SCCACHE_REGION "${SCCACHE_REGION}"
              -e AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID
              -e AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY
              -e SCCACHE_STATS_DIR /workspace/sccache-stats
            )
            LANE_COMMAND=(./scripts/infra/run_with_test_sccache.sh "${LANE_COMMAND[@]}")
          fi
          TEST_RUNNER_ARGS=()
          if [ "${MATRIX_KIND}" = "h100" ]; then
            TEST_RUNNER_ARGS+=(--workers-per-gpu 2)
            # The CPU Unittest lane runs tests/cpu on every run, so the H100
            # lane's tests/ collection leaves it out. ci/bash.sh appends its own
            # --ignore and forwards PYTEST_ADDOPTS into GPU containers.
            export PYTEST_ADDOPTS="${PYTEST_ADDOPTS:+${PYTEST_ADDOPTS} }--ignore=tests/cpu"
          elif [ "${MATRIX_KIND}" = "cpu" ]; then
            # No GPU in the container. ci/bash.sh forwards the lane identity
            # only for GPU containers, so pass it here for summary.py.
            # tests/cpu peaks near 4 GiB host RSS per file on H100, so 16
            # workers fit the CPU runners the AOT lanes use (the arm64 one has
            # 64 vCPU and ~500 GiB). More would not help: the slowest file,
            # about 250 s, sets the floor.
            DOCKER_ARGS+=(
              --no-gpu
              -e CI_GPU_NAME "${CI_GPU_NAME}"
              -e CI_TEST_SCRIPT "${TEST_SCRIPT}"
              -e CI_MATRIX_CUDA "${MATRIX_CUDA}"
            )
            TEST_RUNNER_ARGS+=(--workers 16)
          fi
          # Per-build compile times, summarized by the "Summarize JIT build times"
          # step. Appended: DOCKER_ARGS already carries the sccache settings.
          mkdir -p junit
          DOCKER_ARGS+=(-e FLASHINFER_JIT_BUILD_LOG /workspace/junit/jit-builds.jsonl)
          if [ "${MATRIX_KIND}" = "gpu" ] && [ "${TEST_SCRIPT}" = "task_run_unit_tests.sh" ]; then
            # Targeted T4 runs compile with the same Ninja parallelism as the
            # bare-run T4 script (MAX_JOBS=nproc) instead of test_utils.sh's
            # 12 GB-per-nvcc budget, which was sized for H100 and resolves to
            # MAX_JOBS=1 on these 8-vCPU / 30 GiB runners. The shard scripts have
            # run these files at nproc without an OOM, and a 9-job targeted run of
            # test_batch_prefill_kernels.py peaked at 12.3 GiB process-tree RSS.
            DOCKER_ARGS+=(-e MAX_JOBS "$(nproc)")
          fi
          TEST_TARGETS=()
          if [ -n "${TEST_PATH_ARG:-}" ]; then
            # Read into an array and expand quoted, rather than relying on word
            # splitting: this keeps the shell safe on its own terms instead of
            # inheriting the validator's charset guarantee. Globbing is off for the
            # same reason.
            set -f
            read -r -a TEST_TARGETS <<< "${TEST_PATH_ARG}"
            set +f
          fi
          if [ "${#TEST_TARGETS[@]}" -gt 0 ] && [ "${TEST_SCRIPT}" != "task_run_unit_tests.sh" ]; then
            # A10G shard scripts take no arguments; their pytest wrapper skips files
            # outside JIT_TEST_SCOPE. Comma-joined because ci/bash.sh word-splits
            # -e values.
            DOCKER_ARGS+=(-e JIT_TEST_SCOPE "$(IFS=,; echo "${TEST_TARGETS[*]}")")
            bash ci/bash.sh "${DOCKER_IMAGE}" "${DOCKER_ARGS[@]}" "${LANE_COMMAND[@]}"
          elif [ "${#TEST_TARGETS[@]}" -gt 0 ]; then
            # --test-path, not bare positionals: task_run_unit_tests.sh forwards "$@"
            # to unit_test_runner.py, whose parser takes the scope as an option (or the
            # TEST_PATH env var, which ci/bash.sh does not forward into the container).
            # Bare paths fail argument-preflight with "unrecognized arguments".
            bash ci/bash.sh "${DOCKER_IMAGE}" "${DOCKER_ARGS[@]}" "${LANE_COMMAND[@]}" "${TEST_RUNNER_ARGS[@]}" --test-path "${TEST_TARGETS[@]}"
          else
            bash ci/bash.sh "${DOCKER_IMAGE}" "${DOCKER_ARGS[@]}" "${LANE_COMMAND[@]}" "${TEST_RUNNER_ARGS[@]}"
          fi

      # Runs even when tests fail or the run is cancelled: whatever was
      # compiled is still valid. Credentials are requested only now, so they
      # never reach the test step and stay short-lived.
      - name: Get compile cache upload credentials
        if: always() && env.CI_COMPILE_CACHE_WRITER_DIR != ''
        continue-on-error: true
        uses: aws-actions/configure-aws-credentials@v4
        with:
          role-to-assume: ${{ vars.COMPILE_CACHE_S3_ROLE_ARN }}
          aws-region: ${{ vars.SCCACHE_REGION || 'us-west-2' }}
          role-session-name: compile-cache-${{ github.run_id }}
          role-duration-seconds: 900

      - name: Upload compile cache
        if: always() && env.CI_COMPILE_CACHE_WRITER_DIR != ''
        env:
          S3_BUCKET: ${{ vars.SCCACHE_BUCKET || 'flashinfer-build-cache' }}
        run: |
          # Keyed by the immutable image ID, as ci/compile_cache.sh restores it.
          IMAGE_ID=$(docker image inspect --format '{{.Id}}' "${DOCKER_IMAGE}" 2>/dev/null || true)
          if [[ ${IMAGE_ID} =~ ^sha256:[0-9a-f]{64}$ ]]; then
            bash ci/compile_cache_s3.sh upload "s3://${S3_BUCKET}/compile-cache/main" \
              "${IMAGE_ID#sha256:}" "${CI_COMPILE_CACHE_S3_LANE}" "${CI_COMPILE_CACHE_WRITER_DIR}" || true
          else
            echo "::warning::image ID of ${DOCKER_IMAGE} unavailable; compile cache not uploaded"
          fi
          sudo -n rm -rf "${CI_COMPILE_CACHE_WRITER_DIR}" || rm -rf "${CI_COMPILE_CACHE_WRITER_DIR}" || true

      - name: Display sccache stats
        if: always() && (matrix.kind == 'aot' || env.GPU_TEST_SCCACHE == '1')
        run: |
          STATS_FILE="${GITHUB_WORKSPACE}/sccache-stats/sccache-stats.txt"
          if [ -s "${STATS_FILE}" ]; then
            cat "${STATS_FILE}"
          else
            echo "::warning::sccache stats were not produced"
          fi

      - name: Record sccache job metadata
        if: always() && (matrix.kind == 'aot' || env.GPU_TEST_SCCACHE == '1')
        run: |
          mkdir -p "${GITHUB_WORKSPACE}/sccache-stats"
          IMAGE_DIGESTS=$(docker image inspect --format '{{json .RepoDigests}}' "${DOCKER_IMAGE}" 2>/dev/null || printf 'unavailable')
          {
            printf 'git_commit=%s\n' "$(git rev-parse HEAD)"
            printf 'docker_image=%s\n' "${DOCKER_IMAGE}"
            printf 'docker_image_repo_digests=%s\n' "${IMAGE_DIGESTS}"
            printf 'matrix_cuda=%s\n' "${MATRIX_CUDA}"
            printf 'matrix_arch=%s\n' "${MATRIX_ARCH}"
            printf 'matrix_kind=%s\n' "${MATRIX_KIND}"
            printf 'test_script=%s\n' "${TEST_SCRIPT}"
          } > "${GITHUB_WORKSPACE}/sccache-stats/job-metadata.txt"

      - name: Upload sccache stats
        if: always() && (matrix.kind == 'aot' || env.GPU_TEST_SCCACHE == '1')
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          # GPU lanes share a CUDA/runner pair, so they add the matrix index.
          name: ${{ matrix.kind == 'aot' && format('sccache-stats-{0}-{1}', matrix.cuda, matrix.runner[2]) || format('sccache-stats-{0}-{1}-{2}', matrix.kind, matrix.cuda, strategy.job-index) }}
          path: sccache-stats/
          if-no-files-found: warn
          retention-days: 14

      - name: Summarize JIT build times
        if: always() && matrix.kind != 'aot'
        run: |
          if command -v python3 >/dev/null; then
            python3 scripts/infra/summarize_jit_builds.py junit/jit-builds.jsonl || true
            python3 scripts/infra/summarize_jit_builds.py --markdown \
              junit/jit-builds.jsonl >> "${GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY}" || true
          else
            echo "::warning::python3 unavailable on runner; JIT build summary skipped"
          fi

      - name: Make JUnit XML readable
        if: ${{ always() && matrix.kind != 'aot' }}
        run: |
          if [ -d junit ]; then
            sudo chmod -R a+rX junit
          fi

      - name: Upload JUnit XML and telemetry
        if: ${{ always() && matrix.kind != 'aot' }}
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          # Non-H100 names add the runner SM: A10G and T4 rows can run the same script.
          name: junit-${{ (matrix.kind == 'h100' || matrix.kind == 'cpu') && matrix.kind || format('{0}-{1}', matrix.script, matrix.runner[4]) }}-${{ github.run_id }}-${{ github.run_attempt }}
          path: |
            junit/**/*.xml
            junit/**/*.telemetry.json
            junit/**/*.meta.json
            junit/**/*.results.json
            junit/**/*.log
            junit/**/*.memory.csv
            junit/resource-telemetry/**/*
            junit/memory_summary.csv
            junit/test_timings.csv
            junit/source_summary.csv
            junit/collection-*/*.log
            junit/jit-builds.jsonl
            junit/run-summary.json
          if-no-files-found: warn
          retention-days: 30

      - name: Make shard JUnit XML readable
        if: ${{ always() && matrix.kind == 'gpu' }}
        run: |
          if [ -d junit-shard ]; then
            sudo chmod -R a+rX junit-shard
          fi

      - name: Upload shard JUnit XML
        if: ${{ always() && matrix.kind == 'gpu' }}
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: junit-shard-${{ matrix.name }}-${{ github.run_id }}-${{ github.run_attempt }}
          path: |
            junit-shard/**/*.xml
            junit-shard/**/resource-telemetry/**/*
            junit-shard/**/*.memory.csv
            junit-shard/**/memory_summary.csv
            junit-shard/**/test_timings.csv
            junit-shard/**/source_summary.csv
            junit-shard/**/run-summary.json
            junit-shard/**/*.telemetry.json
            junit-shard/**/*.meta.json
            junit-shard/**/*.results.json
            junit-shard/**/*.log
          if-no-files-found: warn
